LESSON: WRITING 4.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need to write clearly and neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: The learner connects with technology as they use the internet to connect and watch videos on formation of target letters.

Values:
Unity: cooperation is enhanced as learner, in small groups, practise writing 3-4 letter words from left to right

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: effective communication is enhanced as learners use neat and legible handwriting in writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Legible handwriting is emphasised in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Manual alphabet chart, flash cards, internet, posters, online dictionaries, assistive devices fitted with appropriate technologies such as hearing aids and

amplifiers, adapted course books, flash cards, sign language dictionary, internet, signed audio-visual recordings
